Simple add-on parts to modify any diecast car for any postapocalyptic racing game. Scales well with ~1:64 original Matchbox scale. Primarly designed for Gaslands but can be used for any other games as well.

Updates
---------
* **12.7.18:** Started to split this thing into multiple new things with a theme (armour, fuel tanks, etc.) for easier maintenance...
* **23.5.18:** Some very simple straight rams added (PS: forgot some that are not on the photo...).
* **22.5.18:** Motor Prototype added, prints in 3 parts to avoid overhangs (no support needed). Parts will be interchangeable in the future to allow customization and different builds.
* **17.5.18:** Some simple exhaust pipes added...
* **10.5.18:** Barrel and gas can set added. Barrels are very, very thin (1 0.4mm layer) to be able to dent them after printing with a little bit of heat...


Additional elements will be added in a timely manner...
Splitting into separate theme-based things (barrels, rams, armour, motors, etc.) was requested but this will take a little bit of time in reorganization.

[KICKSTARTER ALERT!](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/292543184/scatterblocks)

We're currently running a Kickstarter campaign for the [extended range of our ScatterBlocks](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/292543184/scatterblocks) (quick-assembling miniature terrain), so drop on by and drop us a pledge if you want the full range. For those of you supporting us (or thinking about supporting us) on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames), all the rewards will go to our backers there as well (as we do with all our crowdfunding campaigns).

These OBJ models were designed for use in [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/) to give you a head-start creating gnomish characters. If you import them into [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/), their parts should remain separate and you can immediately begin sculpting and posing them any way you like.

If you make anything with these, let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want! (Psst... we take requests and commissions...)

Enjoy!

This OBJ model was designed for use in [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/) to give you a head-start creating human (or otherwise anthropomorphic) characters, and are what I use as a starter for many of my own miniatures. If you import them into [Sculptris](http://pixologic.com/sculptris/), their parts should remain separate and you can immediately begin sculpting and posing them any way you like.

If you make anything with these, let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested in helping to fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want! (Psst... we take requests and commissions...)

Enjoy!

These STL files are designed to equip my [Sculptris Dummies](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1972042). You won't be able to import these files into Sculptris, though once you get your character posed, you can align these parts in any model staging platform (MakerBot Deskto, Blender, Meshmixer, or 3D Builder are all good choices). All of these parts are also available in Andrew Stockton's awesome [Desktop Hero](https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/263291121/desktophero-free-3d-printable-character-maker) project as well (which is quite a bit easier than adjusting all the parts by hand). All of these weapons have been scaled to 28mm/Heroic scale, so they should be ready for any kind of miniature conversion if you want to print them separately.

If you make anything with these (including through Desktop Hero), let me know and post a link here in the comments section (and certainly post a remix when you have something printable). I'd love to see what you come up with!

You can find an expanding collection of compatible parts [here](https://www.thingiverse.com/dutchmogul/collections/desktop-hero-parts).

I wasn't intending on doing a follow up piece to my previous sculpt, but got inspired by beardly goodness.

Character sculpt at relatively low, medium and high and highest poly counts.

File will need support material, but the top half of the model has been successfully printed on an UP printer, needing relatively low amount of supports. Should work great on a resin/SLA printer. Hoping to do a full test print soon, will see if a manually modelled support structure is needed for the hair. Was just too keen to make the file public and see what the community does with it. :)

Edit: Confirmed printable on FDM! Thanks ichibey!

Edit 2: Uploaded second option for all detail levels with a single shell, mostly to fix issues with the eyes. Thanks 3DWP! Zip file contains all detail levels.

Sculpted in Zbrush, preview renders in Blender, final check and stl file saved from Netfabb.

Approximate poly counts
Low = 137,000 tris
Med = 372,000 tris
High = 965,000 tris
Highest = 2,804,000 tris

This is a Triceratops scan from artec3d.com's gallery. I reduced the mesh from the original and converted the file to STL.

This model requires supports, but the support marks aren't too much of a problem since they're out of sight on the underside and the skin texture also hides them.

I kept the mesh resolution high enough that you should be able to scale this even larger with good results. The size of this model is about 7 inches long by 3 inches high, and I estimate that my Replicator 2 could print it up to 50% larger.

As famine struck the dark forests of Jotunheim, Wolf-Eater scaled the impossible cliffs of Ymir's Brow, descending into the lowlands of Midgard and sating his hunger on the tribes of men.

I wanted to make a proper Norse dragon. I really liked the idea of an antlered forest wyrm with vestigial wings adapted to climbing giant trees. Currently using this guy as the center of an RPG storyline. He's scaled to 15mm (making him rather massive) so he can be used with my Pocket-Tactics models, but he'd make a good dragon for heroic scale (25-30mm gaming) as well.
